candidates.label: Thyatira archaeological remains (Akhisar)
candidates.support: Thyatira, in the region of Lydia, is undisputed as continuous with modern Akhisar; Pleiades and Wikidata's coordinates for the site agree closely.

summary.text: Thyatira was a Lydian city on a tributary of the Hermus river, known from inscriptions for its trade guilds. Acts identifies Lydia, the first convert baptized at Philippi, as 'a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira,' and Thyatira is also one of the seven churches addressed in Revelation 2, commended for love and service but rebuked for tolerating a false prophetess.

scripture.textWEB: A certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, one who worshiped God, heard us. The Lord opened her heart to listen to the things which were spoken by Paul.
